messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — ran a smoke perf sweep on the fused-RoPE path with KV prefetch + adaptive batching enabled and saw a 20% tail latency regression on short sequences (<=32). attaching the micro-bench output below.

kevin: hmm, did you hit FlashAttention2 or the paged attention path?

anna: By default it selected flash2 for seq<=64, but the runtime fell back to paged when prefetch triggered >1 page. I forced flash2 and the regression disappears.

sophia: can you paste the config you used? curious about the batching window + prefetch threshold.

anna: config snippet:
```
serve.runtime.batch_window_ms=12
kv.prefetch_pages=2
kernel.selection.policy=cost_latency
kernel.force=null
```
The issue repros when kv.prefetch_pages=2. If set to 0 it's fine but that kills throughput.

mike: summary from micro-bench: flash2 path p95=18ms, paged-attn p95=34ms when prefetching pages overlaps with batch flush. CPU spin+copy into pinned buf seems to cause stalls.

kevin: sounds like our kernel selector's cost model doesn't account for the extra copy latency when rotary dims are scaled. Are you using scaled RoPE or fused RoPE with dim folding?

anna: fused RoPE with rotary_dim_scale=1.2 for the larger heads (we're doing dim scaling to stabilize training transfer). That increases per-head GEMM size and the page layout changes.

sophia: possible fix: add a heuristic to prefer flash variants if rotary_dim_scale != 1 and seq <= 64 and prefetch_pages <=1. Also consider marking prefetch as asynchronous (dont block batch flush).

mike: +1 on async prefetch. Also we should add a microbench in CI that flips prefetcht=0/1/2 and runs short-seq workload. Catches regressions fast.

kevin: I can prototype selector change: budget an extra memcpy cost when prefetched_pages>0 and rotary_dim_scale!=1. Then prefer flash if expected added cost > threshold.

perf-bot: perf artifact uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/1977778888/bench.html (flamegraphs + raw.csv) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anna: thanks — i'll attach a minimized repro and try the selector patch locally. If it looks good i'll open a PR with the microbench and the selector heuristic.

sophia: one more note — quantify impact on tokens/sec not just p95. Prefetch increased throughput by ~8% in long seq (>512) tests but hurts short tails. need a policy knob.

mike: propose exposing runtime knobs: kernel.prefer_low_tail = <bool|auto>, kv.prefetch_mode = <sync|async|off>. Then default to auto which uses selector heuristic.

anna: agreed. i'll start with a non-invasive selector change + async prefetch opt. will post results here. :thumbsup:
